answer: Admission turns on one bridge: an applicant must show a signal of work with two unconnected groups — a pearl, like a joint tool or report, with a distinct part by the applicant. A coordinator from each side checks within seven days that it is original and the groups share no members or funding. If either check fails, or the same pearl appears under another name, it is refused and both coordinators are barred for six months. One honest applicant needs only the bridge they already use; forging a thousand means a thousand separate collaborations.
